title: GADGETSPINNER: A New Transient Execution Primitive Using the Loop Stream Detector
problem: Modern out-of-order CPUs have unexploited transient execution vulnerabilities in the Loop Stream Detector (LSD), which retains stale branch predictions across loop iterations and enables speculative out-of-bounds execution and information leakage.
motivation: Transient execution attacks are a critical security threat to all modern CPUs, and existing transient execution defenses fail against LSD-based attacks.
method: The Loop Stream Detector is a CPU component that remembers which direction a branch went in the first iteration of a loop and keeps reusing that prediction for subsequent iterations without checking if it's correct. GADGETSPINNER exploits this by forcing the CPU to speculatively execute (run code before confirming it's the right path) beyond the loop's boundary using the outdated prediction. While executing the wrong code, illegal operations run and leak confidential information before the CPU realizes its prediction was wrong.
key_novelty: This is the first attack exploiting how the Loop Stream Detector reuses branch predictions across loop iterations, causing the CPU to speculatively execute outside the loop's intended boundary and leak confidential data.
